common_name: Emperor of China Chrysanthemum (Fully Double Silvery-Pink Quilled Petals)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Emperor of China is a fully double, silvery-pink, quilled-petal heirloom chrysanthemum on a tall 3-4 foot plant.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Emperor of China, a long-cultivated heirloom, bears fully double flowers with narrow, quilled, silvery-pink petals on a tall, vigorous plant that also produces attractive bronze-red fall foliage color, a distinctive dual-season interest rare among garden mums. Pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth, since unpinched plants tend toward tall, floppy stems. Divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding and maintain vigor.

common_name: Duchess of Edinburgh Chrysanthemum (Semi-Double Bright Red with Yellow Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Duchess of Edinburgh bears semi-double, bright red flowers with a yellow eye.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Duchess of Edinburgh bears semi-double flowers in bright, warm red with a contrasting yellow center eye, giving the open flower form a two-tone effect uncommon among the more solid-colored garden mum cultivars. Pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth, since unpinched plants tend toward tall, floppy stems. Divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding and maintain vigor.

common_name: Cambodian Queen Chrysanthemum (Lavender-Flowered Sport of Sheffield Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Cambodian Queen is a lavender-flowered sport of Sheffield Pink, discovered at Creek Hill Nursery in Pennsylvania.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil; Cambodian Queen blooms equally well in partial shade. A lavender-flowered sport discovered at Creek Hill Nursery in Pennsylvania on the popular Sheffield Pink, Cambodian Queen produces large, single, daisy-form flowers in soft lavender rather than its parent's salmon-pink, blooming late in the season and providing fall color when most summer perennials are exhausted. Divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding, and pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth.

common_name: Gethsemane Moonlight Chrysanthemum (Semi-Double Primrose-Yellow, Rapidly Spreading)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Gethsemane Moonlight bears semi-double, primrose-yellow daisies on a rapidly spreading clump.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Gethsemane Moonlight bears semi-double, soft primrose-yellow daisy flowers on a plant that spreads notably faster and more vigorously than many other hardy mum cultivars, quickly filling in a naturalized area or informal border with cheerful late-season color. Divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding and control its enthusiastic spread, and pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Nantyderry Sunshine bears amber-yellow, button/pompon-form flowerheads and is listed among the RHS's top 200 garden plants.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Nantyderry Sunshine, recognized by the Royal Horticultural Society among its top 200 garden plants, bears small, tightly formed, amber-yellow button and pompon-form flowerheads in great abundance, a fine-textured, densely floriferous display distinct from the larger single or double daisy forms of many other hardy mum cultivars. Divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding, and pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth.

common_name: Anastasia Chrysanthemum (Spider-Form Mum with Long Curling Petals)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Anastasia is a spider-form mum with long, curling ray florets, grown commercially in pink, bronze, lavender, white, and green.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil; spider mums generally need more sun and staking support than compact garden mum types. Anastasia bears large, dramatic spider-form flowers with long, narrow, curling ray florets that give the bloom a fireworks-like, wispy appearance, sold commercially in pink, bronze, lavender, white, and green color forms and grown chiefly for cutting rather than garden display. Stake plants to support the tall stems and heavy flower heads, and disbud side buds if larger, showier terminal blooms are the goal.

common_name: Symphony Chrysanthemum (Exhibition Spider Mum, Feathery Russet-Orange-Bronze)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Symphony is an exhibition spider mum with long, feathery russet-orange-bronze petals.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil; spider mums generally need more sun and staking support than compact garden mum types. Symphony, a favorite exhibition spider mum, bears long, feathery, curling petals in warm russet-orange-to-bronze tones, prized on the show bench for the elegant, flowing form of its petals, which distinguish spider mums from the tighter, more compact button and decorative garden mum types. Stake plants to support the tall stems and heavy flower heads, and disbud side buds if larger, showier terminal blooms are the goal.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Grandchild is an award-winning, double, reflexed mauve-pink chrysanthemum on a hardy bushy perennial.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Grandchild bears fully double, reflexed flowers in soft mauve-pink, the petals curving gracefully backward toward the stem in the classic reflexed form, on a hardy, bushy perennial that has earned recognition among garden mum enthusiasts for its reliable performance and refined bloom shape. Pinch stem tips in spring and early summer to promote bushy, compact growth, and divide clumps every two to three years to prevent crowding and maintain vigor.
